thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed for model-runner-prod (us-west-2) starting 02:09 UTC. Error rate jump: 0.8% -> 9.6% on /v1/generate. Paging on-call: @mike.

Mike (on-call): ack. I'm on it. Seeing spikes on the dashboard. Rolling pager. Lina, any customer comms? Ryan/Sam, can you grab logs and whether this is a scaling event vs crash?

Lina (support): got three tickets from two enterprise customers — sessions failing with `5xx: model runtime unavailable` and `timeout waiting for response`. Sharing one stack from support logs: `POST /v1/generate 500 "runtime error: signal 11"`.

Ryan (eng-runtime): thanks. Signal 11 suggests a segfault in the native runtime. Pulling recent deploys... I see a canary rollout of runtime-v2.4.7 at 02:05 UTC to ~10% of instances. That could map.

Sam (infra): host-level metrics show a sharp GPU mem + host RSS spike on the affected pods right before the 5xxs. Kernel dmesg on one host:

```
[Feb 18 02:07:14] Out of memory: Kill process 24321 (model-runner) total-vm:4123456kB, anon-rss:3890120kB, file-rss:0kB
[Feb 18 02:07:14] Killed process 24321 (model-runner) total-vm:4123456kB
```

Sam (infra): also seeing OOM killer more frequently than baseline on that instance group. Noticed recent node kernel patch last week, but only the runtime rollout lines up exactly.

Mike (on-call): good context. If it's a new runtime causing memory leaks/overflow under certain seq lengths we should rollback canary and reroute traffic off the canary pods. Can infra reroute traffic away from canary pool? @sam

Sam (infra): initiating emergency routing — moving traffic off tag=runtime-v2.4.7 canary. Command I used:

```
/ops/reroute --cluster us-west-2 --tag runtime-v2.4.7 --action drain
```

Sam (infra): done for cluster us-west-2-canary. Observability note: added temporary verbose core dump collection to /var/crash/model-runner/.

Ryan (eng-runtime): I’m attaching a lightweight fix: disabling async KV cache for the canary so memory footprint reduces. Patch: `disable_kvcache_on_start=true` in runtime flags. Kicking a hot-restart to affected pods.

Mike (on-call): Lina — let customers know we are investigating and routing around canary. Use the standard incident line: "We're experiencing increased 5xxs; engineering is investigating; temporary mitigation in progress."

Lina (support): firing update to impacted customers now. Template: "we're routing traffic to stable instances and monitoring. ETA for resolution: 15-30 mins; we'll follow up with root cause." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Ryan (eng-runtime): snipped portion of one core dump backtrace (symbols stripped):

```
#0  0x7f2a3b12 in ?? ()
#1  0x7f2a4e22 in kv_cache_update ()
#2  0x559c1f34 in model_infer ()
#3  0x559c2b11 in runner_loop ()
```

Ryan (eng-runtime): looks like kv_cache update path is implicated on big prefix sizes. I’ll instrument more and add guard rails to cap allocation. For immediate mitigation we've rolled back traffic and restarted canary pods with KV cache disabled.

Sam (infra): after draining canary and restarting, host OOM events dropped. Metrics now show error rate sliding down; from 9.6% -> 3.2% over the last 6 mins.

Mike (on-call): good. Continue to monitor. Any need to scale cluster or expand reroute to other regions?

Ryan (eng-runtime): not yet. I want a full rollback of v2.4.7 from canary to stop any remaining small-volume traffic. Also will OOM-protect: cap sequence length at gateway layer for now (max_seq=2048) until we push a memory-safe runtime.

Sam (infra): done: rollback request submitted and gateway caps applied with `--max_seq=2048`. Propagated configs to us-west-2 in 80s.

Lina (support): customers acknowledged and appreciate proactive routing. No new severity escalations in the last 10 mins.

Zoe (product): tracking which customers hit the large sequences — is this correlated with a new feature enabling longer contexts? If so we may want a product-side flag.

Ryan (eng-runtime): quick note: we reproduced a mem spike locally by sending a request with many tool calls and long prefix. We’ll ship a patch that does two things: (1) guard allocations in kv cache; (2) fallback to streaming token-by-token when memory estimate > threshold. Target ETA: 4 hours for hotfix branch, 24 hours for full safe rollout after QA.

Mike (on-call): plan for now: 1) confirm error rate returns to baseline (target <1%). 2) keep canary drained. 3) emergency rollback completed. 4) support/customer comms sent. 5) schedule postmortem with infra/eng/runtime/product. Any objections?

Sam (infra): no objections. I'll keep extra alerts on for 2 hrs and hold the rollback until eng announces the safe build.

Ryan (eng-runtime): posting quick repro steps for the postmortem and follow-up tickets:

- repro.sh -> sends 4 concurrent long-prefix inferences
- collect: /var/crash/model-runner/*.core and `kubectl logs` for restarted pods
- metrics: `gpu_mem_used`, `host_rss_bytes`, `kvcache_size` on time series

Mike (on-call): metrics show further drop: 3.2% -> 0.9% over the last 8 mins. Routing appears effective. Marking incident as mitigated — continuing to observe.

IncidentBot: Status update: incident_state=mitigated, impacted_percent=~0.6, notification=customers-updated. Pager cleared.

Lina (support): sending final follow-up to impacted customers: "issue mitigated; engineering is working on root cause and patch; we'll update with ETA for fix." :white_check_mark:

Ryan (eng-runtime): creating PR with cap and allocation guards now. I’ll tag for rapid QA. Postmortem owner: me. Mike, Sam, Lina, Zoe — please add any additional notes you want in postmortem.

Mike (on-call): thanks team. I’ll write up initial timeline and hand over to Ryan for postmortem. Leaving the channel open for now in case of regressions.

Sam (infra): keeping watch. If OOMs reappear I’ll escalate immediately.

Zoe (product): scheduling customer follow-up sync for tomorrow to discuss sequence-length controls and UX flags.

Mike (on-call): incident thread closing in 2h unless new alerts come in. Great job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:
